text: What is the general structure common to Gettier's 1963 counterexamples that shows justified true belief is not sufficient for knowledge?
choices: S justifiably infers a true proposition from a justified but false lemma, so S's belief is true only by luck rather than because of the supporting evidence.
S believes a true proposition but has no justification whatsoever for it, so the belief is a mere lucky guess.
S holds a well-justified belief that turns out to be false, showing that justification does not guarantee truth.
S fails to believe a proposition that is both true and well justified, so the belief condition goes unmet.
explanation: In each Gettier case S validly and justifiably infers a truth q from a justified proposition p that is in fact false; q happens to be true, but for reasons unconnected to S's evidence, so the true belief is only accidentally true. All three JTB conditions are met yet knowledge is absent. Option 1 describes a mere lucky guess (no justification at all) and option 2 describes an ordinary justified false belief, neither of which is the Gettier structure.
